newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mori, Shinshin agree on business, equity link.
newsitem.headline: Mori, Shinshin agree on business, equity link.

text.p: Mori Denki Manufacturing Co Ltd said on Thursday that it had agreed on a business and equity tie-up with shopping centre operator Shinshin Shoji KK.

Industrial lighting equipment maker Mori and Shinshin will combine their knowhow and conduct a joint research and development project on the effective operation of shopping centres, Mori said in a statement.
The impact of the tie-up on Mori's sales was not immediately known, Mori said.
It said the tie-up was decided in view of Mori's recent poor business performance, and to improve the company's financial health.
It said it would issue eight million new shares in a third party allotment to Shinshin president Shodai Nitta.
The new shares will be issued on November 19, Mori said.
The issue price will be 415 yen per share and the number of outstanding shares will total 30.20 million after the issue.
As Nitta already holds 1.2 million shares, he would become Mori's largest shareholder after the issue, holding a 30.5 percent stake, Mori said.
Mori also said that Bunka Shutter Co Ltd had sold four million of its five million Mori shares to Nitta and the Shinshin group.
Bunka Shutter was the largest shareholder in Mori before the sale, Mori said.
